accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem 1: sharp effect frontier
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The frontier is conditional on a fixed normalized OICA representation and on source-minimal monomial disturbance assignment; it is not claimed invariant to source splitting, duplicated sources, or alternative normalized representations of the same observed law.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Sharp over the stated fiber \(\mathfrak F_x(C,\varepsilon)\), conditional on the fixed representation \((C,\varepsilon)\).

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorem 3: uniform confidence frontier
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The finite-sample statement is conditional on the nonempty separated common-order OICA class and iid sampling; it does not cover the Hong Kong time series or source-specific cumulant orders.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Uniform \(1-\alpha\) coverage and root-\(N\) informative-regime radius only over \(\mathfrak P_{p,n,r}(a,\delta,\sigma,\kappa,\Lambda,M)\).

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper characterizes distributional equivalence of latent cyclic LiNG models, gives an equivalence-class traversal/recovery pipeline, and reports a 14-stock, two-latent-variable class with 19,008 graphs; it does not state a fixed-numerical-mixing-fiber equilibrium-effect image.

The paper studies generic direct and total effect identification in acyclic latent-variable LiNGAMs, provides complete graphical characterizations, and proposes certification algorithms and a graph-known estimation procedure.
The article gives an if-and-only-if characterization of OICA identifiability and a coupled matrix/tensor recovery method; it does not study the causal completion fiber or its effect frontier.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper establishes overcomplete tensor-learning and perturbation/concentration guarantees under its own incoherence and initialization conditions, including ICA applications, but not downstream causal-set coverage.

The paper treats overcomplete ICA through Hessians of the cumulant-generating function and an SDP relaxation for component recovery, not source-specific finite-order alignment or causal-set inference.

The work jointly uses third and fourth cumulants for a square, nonsingular independent-component model and develops associated estimating procedures; it does not address overcomplete OICA or the proposed causal frontier.
